summary: Feed s171_triple to SIEM is degraded: 3 faults detected. High-severity tool overload (3.62 Gbps bursts vs 1 Gbps port) and oversize frames (5.6% >1518B, dropped by NIC) cause traffic loss/blind spots, plus medium-severity duplicates (7.4%) waste SIEM capacity.

findings.root_cause: Microbursts peaking at 3.62 Gbps overwhelm the 1 Gbps SIEM ingress port (362% of capacity across 9 intervals). Likely single-tool-port delivery from packet broker without load-balancing or burst buffering for aggregated SPAN/TAP feeds.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM port buffers overflow and drops packets during bursts, causing missed events, incomplete flows, and gaps in detection/coverage despite no broker-level drops reported.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute bursts across multiple 1 Gbps SIEM inputs or a higher-capacity port group to keep peak <80% utilization; SIEM does not need both directions so per-flow hashing preserves event integrity.

findings.root_cause: Upstream jumbo/MTU 8058-byte frames forwarded unchanged by packet broker; SIEM NIC max is 1518 bytes so it drops them. 207/3725 frames (5.6%) exceed MTU.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM NIC silently drops 5.6% of frames, creating blind spot for large-frame flows; security events carried in those frames are never ingested.

recommended_fix.why: Tool profile needs_full_payload=false, so broker-side slicing/trimming to 1518B preserves headers for SIEM detection while fitting port MTU and avoiding NIC drops.

findings.root_cause: 7.4% duplicate packets (276/3725) indicates same traffic arriving via multiple SPAN/mirror paths or TAP aggregation without broker deduplication.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM wastes CPU/storage on duplicate events, inflates EPS/license count, and risks false correlation/alert duplication without improving coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to remove identical packets before delivery, cutting 7.4% waste while preserving unique events for SIEM.
